<style>
/* Small centered blue label, used on every section heading below. Applied
   via a Pandoc heading attribute (## Heading {.about-eyebrow}) so each one
   stays a real <h2> for document structure, and only its presentation
   changes.

   Must stay scoped to h2: with _quarto.yml's section-divs, Pandoc copies a
   heading's classes onto the <section> wrapper it generates as well as onto
   the heading itself, so a bare `.about-eyebrow` selector also matches the
   whole section — and every inheritable property here (color, text-align,
   text-transform, letter-spacing, font-weight) then cascades into that
   section's body paragraphs.

   The !important on font-size overrides Quarto's own heading scale, which
   is set on the element and would otherwise win. */
h2.about-eyebrow {
  text-align: center;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  font-size: 0.78rem !important;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #2563eb;
  margin: 2.75rem 0 0.75rem;
  border-bottom: none;
}

.about-hero-lead {
  max-width: 640px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  text-align: center;
  font-size: 1.1rem;
  line-height: 1.6;
  color: var(--bs-secondary-color, #475569);
}

.about-visual {
  max-width: 460px;
  margin: 1.75rem auto 2rem;
}

.about-visual-plot {
  width: 100%;
  height: 260px;
  filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 6px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.1));
}

/* Rotation between the three illustration scenes below. Each scene's own
   internal animations keep their independent 12s duration/keyframes
   unchanged; because 36s / 12s = 3 exactly, every scene's internal loop
   is always back at its own phase 0 the instant the wrapper reveals it,
   so no rescaling of any scene's internal percentages is needed. */
.about-scene {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-duration: 36s;
  animation-timing-function: linear;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-scene-newton { animation-name: about-scene-newton; }
.about-scene-kalman { animation-name: about-scene-kalman; }
.about-scene-sperner { animation-name: about-scene-sperner; }

@keyframes about-scene-newton {
  0%, 32% { opacity: 1; }
  33% { opacity: 0; }
  100% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-scene-kalman {
  0%, 33% { opacity: 0; }
  34%, 65% { opacity: 1; }
  66% { opacity: 0; }
  100% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-scene-sperner {
  0%, 66% { opacity: 0; }
  67%, 99% { opacity: 1; }
  100% { opacity: 0; }
}

/* Newton's-method loop: exactly one stage is visible at a time (point0,
   then each tangent+point group), crossfading into the next on a shared
   12s cycle so they stay in phase forever without any JS driving them.
   Within each group, the tangent/guide lines "draw" in via a moving
   stroke-dashoffset and the new point pops in with a small scale
   overshoot, layered on top of the parent group's opacity crossfade.
   A plain opacity crossfade is low-risk motion, so it's left running
   even under prefers-reduced-motion. */
.about-newton-point0,
.about-newton-group1,
.about-newton-group2,
.about-newton-group3 {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-duration: 12s;
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-newton-point0 { animation-name: about-newton-point0; transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; }
.about-newton-group1 { animation-name: about-newton-group1; }
.about-newton-group2 { animation-name: about-newton-group2; }
.about-newton-group3 { animation-name: about-newton-group3; }

.about-newton-draw1, .about-newton-draw2, .about-newton-draw3 {
  animation-duration: 12s;
  animation-timing-function: ease-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-newton-pop1, .about-newton-pop2, .about-newton-pop3 {
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: center;
  animation-duration: 12s;
  animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-newton-draw1 { animation-name: about-newton-draw1; }
.about-newton-draw2 { animation-name: about-newton-draw2; }
.about-newton-draw3 { animation-name: about-newton-draw3; }
.about-newton-pop1 { animation-name: about-newton-pop1; }
.about-newton-pop2 { animation-name: about-newton-pop2; }
.about-newton-pop3 { animation-name: about-newton-pop3; }

@keyframes about-newton-point0 {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.3); }
  5% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.15); }
  8%, 17% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
  23% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes about-newton-group1 {
  0%, 17%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  23%, 35% { opacity: 1; }
  41% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-newton-group2 {
  0%, 35%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  41%, 53% { opacity: 1; }
  59% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-newton-group3 {
  0%, 53%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  59%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-newton-draw1 {
  0%, 23% { stroke-dashoffset: 160; }
  29%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-newton-draw2 {
  0%, 41% { stroke-dashoffset: 160; }
  47%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-newton-draw3 {
  0%, 59% { stroke-dashoffset: 160; }
  65%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-newton-pop1 {
  0%, 27% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  32% { transform: scale(1.18); }
  35%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes about-newton-pop2 {
  0%, 45% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  50% { transform: scale(1.18); }
  53%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes about-newton-pop3 {
  0%, 63% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  69% { transform: scale(1.25); }
  73%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

/* Noisy-to-smooth filter loop: the scattered measurements fade in first,
   then the filtered estimate draws itself across left to right via a
   moving stroke-dashoffset, holds, then everything fades out together.
   Same 12s internal duration as the Newton scene, for the same reason. */
.about-kalman-dots, .about-kalman-smooth {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-duration: 12s;
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-kalman-dots { animation-name: about-kalman-dots; }
.about-kalman-smooth { animation-name: about-kalman-smooth; }

@keyframes about-kalman-dots {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  8%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  92% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-kalman-smooth {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; stroke-dashoffset: 680; }
  8% { opacity: 1; stroke-dashoffset: 680; }
  13% { stroke-dashoffset: 680; }
  55% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  83% { opacity: 1; stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  92% { opacity: 0; stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

/* Sperner's-lemma loop: the triangle assembles itself piece by piece
   (outer edges, corner colors, inner subdivision, midpoint colors, then
   the trichromatic triangle highlight), holds the complete picture, then
   fades out together. Same 12s internal duration as the other scenes. */
.about-sperner-outer, .about-sperner-corners, .about-sperner-inner, .about-sperner-mid-dots, .about-sperner-highlight {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-duration: 12s;
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-sperner-draw-outer, .about-sperner-draw-inner {
  animation-duration: 12s;
  animation-timing-function: ease-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-sperner-pop-outer, .about-sperner-pop-inner {
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: center;
  animation-duration: 12s;
  animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.about-sperner-highlight { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; }

.about-sperner-outer { animation-name: about-sperner-outer; }
.about-sperner-corners { animation-name: about-sperner-corners; }
.about-sperner-inner { animation-name: about-sperner-inner; }
.about-sperner-mid-dots { animation-name: about-sperner-mid-dots; }
.about-sperner-highlight { animation-name: about-sperner-highlight, about-sperner-highlight-pop; }
.about-sperner-draw-outer { animation-name: about-sperner-draw-outer; }
.about-sperner-draw-inner { animation-name: about-sperner-draw-inner; }
.about-sperner-pop-outer { animation-name: about-sperner-pop-outer; }
.about-sperner-pop-inner { animation-name: about-sperner-pop-inner; }

@keyframes about-sperner-outer {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  1%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-draw-outer {
  0%, 1% { stroke-dashoffset: 220; }
  15%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-corners {
  0%, 10%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  13%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-pop-outer {
  0%, 10% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  15% { transform: scale(1.2); }
  18%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-inner {
  0%, 15%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  17%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-draw-inner {
  0%, 17% { stroke-dashoffset: 110; }
  30%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-mid-dots {
  0%, 28%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  31%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-pop-inner {
  0%, 28% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  34% { transform: scale(1.2); }
  37%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-highlight {
  0%, 33%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  40%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes about-sperner-highlight-pop {
  0%, 33% { transform: scale(0.5); }
  40% { transform: scale(1.15); }
  44%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}
</style>

## How it works {.about-eyebrow}

Mathematics is full of ideas that come alive the moment you can see them move. Visual Math Lab makes them touchable: pick a function, drag a slider, change a starting guess, and watch the idea unfold one step at a time — from root finding and differential equations to probability, model fitting, and combinatorial proofs.

Explore on your own, use a page as a lecture demo, or hand one to students as a lab. Everything here is open source, so it is yours to fork, adapt, and extend.

## See it in action {.about-eyebrow}

Below is a small taste of what most pages here looks like. 


```{ojs}
//| output: false
// VM is the shared utility library, loaded globally via _includes/head-scripts.html (js/**). This mini demo uses VM.expressions.makeFunctionOfT, VM.expressions.makeNumber, VM.plotting.paddedRange, VM.ui.applyExampleParams.
VM = window.VM
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// plotterExamples backs the "Try an example" dropdown below -- each one is a
// named curve, and between them they demonstrate the ways a parametric
// expression can be phrased.
plotterExamples = [
  {
    title: "Butterfly curve",
    params: {x: "sin(t) * (exp(cos(t)) - 2*cos(4*t) - sin(t/12)^5)", y: "cos(t) * (exp(cos(t)) - 2*cos(4*t) - sin(t/12)^5)", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    // A parametric path doesn't have to be smooth -- ternaries let one
    // formula switch between pieces, here tracing the four sides of a
    // square as t runs 0 -> 4.
    title: "Piecewise: square path",
    params: {x: "t < 1 ? t : (t < 2 ? 1 : (t < 3 ? 3 - t : 0))", y: "t < 1 ? 0 : (t < 2 ? t - 1 : (t < 3 ? 1 : 4 - t))", tmin: "0", tmax: "4"}
  },
  {
    title: "Lissajous curve (3:4)",
    params: {x: "sin(3*t)", y: "sin(4*t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Rose (five petals)",
    params: {x: "cos(5*t) * cos(t)", y: "cos(5*t) * sin(t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Cardioid",
    params: {x: "(1 - cos(t)) * cos(t)", y: "(1 - cos(t)) * sin(t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Astroid",
    params: {x: "cos(t)^3", y: "sin(t)^3", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Lemniscate of Bernoulli",
    params: {x: "cos(t) / (1 + sin(t)^2)", y: "sin(t) * cos(t) / (1 + sin(t)^2)", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Spirograph (epitrochoid)",
    params: {x: "6*cos(t) - 3*cos(6*t)", y: "6*sin(t) - 3*sin(6*t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Deltoid",
    params: {x: "2*cos(t) + cos(2*t)", y: "2*sin(t) - sin(2*t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Archimedean spiral",
    params: {x: "t * cos(t)", y: "t * sin(t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "8*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Cycloid",
    params: {x: "t - sin(t)", y: "1 - cos(t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "6*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Heart curve",
    params: {x: "16*sin(t)^3", y: "13*cos(t) - 5*cos(2*t) - 2*cos(3*t) - cos(4*t)", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Squircle (superellipse)",
    params: {x: "sign(cos(t)) * abs(cos(t))^0.5", y: "sign(sin(t)) * abs(sin(t))^0.5", tmin: "0", tmax: "2*pi"}
  },
  {
    title: "Ordinary graph y = f(x)",
    params: {x: "t", y: "t^3 - 3*t", tmin: "-2.2", tmax: "2.2"}
  }
]
```

```{ojs}
// Matches the colors plotterMainPlot draws each trace in, so the overlay
// legend's swatches double as a color key.
// vmTheme is what makes the colors below reactive. The chart's own chrome
// (background, axes, gridlines) repaints on a dark-mode toggle by itself,
// via the relayout patch in plotly-fullscreen-button.js -- but the *trace*
// colors are values this page bakes into the traces it builds, so nothing
// repaints them unless mainPlot re-runs. Depending on vmTheme is what
// re-runs it. See VM.plotting.onThemeChange for why it fires a couple of
// frames after the toggle rather than inline.
vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))

chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)

plotterTraceColors = new Map([
  ["Curve", chartColors.fn],
  ["Point at t", chartColors.alt]
])
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Applies the selected example's params to the fields above and clicks
// Plot, in place. A plain "change" listener attached once to the stable
// native <select> (rather than an OJS cell reactive on
// plotterExampleSelect's value) -- a <select> fires both "input" and
// "change" per selection, and a reactive cell would run twice, with the
// two overlapping calls racing each other.
applyPlotterExampleFromSelect = {
  const nativeSelect = (viewof plotterExampleSelect).querySelector("select")
  if (!nativeSelect) return
  nativeSelect.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const example = (viewof plotterExampleSelect).value
    if (!example) return
    VM.ui.applyExampleParams(plotterFieldSelectors, example.params, viewof plotterTrigger)
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Pressing Enter in the formula/parameter-range fields clicks Plot instead
// of submitting the field's own (invisible) form.
enterToPlotterPlot = {
  for (const view of [viewof plotterXText, viewof plotterYText, viewof plotterTMin, viewof plotterTMax]) {
    const input = view.querySelector("input")
    if (!input) continue
    input.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
      if (e.key !== "Enter") return
      e.preventDefault()
      viewof plotterTrigger.querySelector("button").click()
    })
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// plotterCommitted snapshots the fields only when Plot is clicked -- it
// reads the stable `viewof` DOM views, not the reactive values, so it does
// not rerun on every keystroke.
plotterCommitted = {
  plotterTrigger
  const math = window.math
  return {
    xText: (viewof plotterXText).value,
    yText: (viewof plotterYText).value,
    tMin: VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, (viewof plotterTMin).value),
    tMax: VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, (viewof plotterTMax).value)
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// plotterSetup samples (x(t), y(t)) across the committed t-range. `key`
// changes whenever a new curve is committed, and is used as the plot's
// uirevision so a fresh curve autoscales instead of inheriting the
// previous curve's zoom.
plotterSetup = {
  const math = window.math
  const x = VM.expressions.makeFunctionOfT(math, plotterCommitted.xText)
  const y = VM.expressions.makeFunctionOfT(math, plotterCommitted.yText)

  let tMin = plotterCommitted.tMin
  let tMax = plotterCommitted.tMax
  const key = JSON.stringify(plotterCommitted)

  if (!x || !y || !Number.isFinite(tMin) || !Number.isFinite(tMax) || tMin === tMax) {
    return {ts: [], xs: [], ys: [], tMin: 0, tMax: 1, xRange: {lo: -1, hi: 1}, yRange: {lo: -1, hi: 1}, key}
  }
  if (tMin > tMax) { const temp = tMin; tMin = tMax; tMax = temp }

  // Parametric curves double back on themselves, so they need a good deal
  // more samples than a graph over an interval before the polyline stops
  // looking faceted.
  const sampleCount = 2400
  const ts = []
  const xs = []
  const ys = []
  for (let i = 0; i < sampleCount; i++) {
    const t = tMin + (tMax - tMin) * i / (sampleCount - 1)
    const xValue = x(t)
    const yValue = y(t)
    ts.push(t)
    if (Number.isFinite(xValue) && Number.isFinite(yValue) && Math.abs(xValue) < 1e8 && Math.abs(yValue) < 1e8) {
      xs.push(xValue)
      ys.push(yValue)
    } else {
      // A null in both coordinates breaks the trace here instead of
      // drawing a spurious segment across a pole or a gap in the domain.
      xs.push(null)
      ys.push(null)
    }
  }

  // Padded explicitly rather than left to Plotly's autorange: an axis pair
  // tied together by scaleanchor (see plotterMainPlot) autoranges with no
  // padding at all on the constraining axis, which put the square path
  // example's two vertical sides exactly on the plot's edges.
  const xRange = VM.plotting.paddedRange(xs, {relativePadding: 0.06, minPadding: 0.1})
  const yRange = VM.plotting.paddedRange(ys, {relativePadding: 0.06, minPadding: 0.1})
  return {ts, xs, ys, tMin, tMax, xRange, yRange, key}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// plotterMainPlot is a closure over a _plotDiv variable so the same DOM
// node is reused across reactive re-renders, preserving zoom/pan.
plotterMainPlot = {
  const Plotly = window.Plotly
  let _plotDiv = null

  return ({ts, xs, ys, xRange, yRange, key}, cursorIndex, showCurve, showCursor) => {
    const data = []

    if (showCurve) {
      data.push({
        x: xs, y: ys, type: "scatter", mode: "lines", name: "Curve", showlegend: false,
        line: {color: chartColors.fn, width: 2.5, shape: "spline"},
        customdata: ts,
        hovertemplate: "t = %{customdata:.3f}<br>x = %{x:.3f}<br>y = %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>"
      })
    }

    // The cursor reads straight out of the sampled arrays rather than
    // re-evaluating x(t)/y(t), so the marker always sits exactly on the
    // polyline that's drawn, never a hair off it.
    const i = cursorIndex
    if (showCursor && i !== null && i >= 0 && i < xs.length && xs[i] !== null) {
      data.push({
        x: [xs[i]], y: [ys[i]], type: "scatter", mode: "markers", name: "Point at t", showlegend: false,
        marker: {color: chartColors.alt, size: 12, line: {color: chartColors.halo, width: 2}},
        customdata: [ts[i]],
        hovertemplate: "t = %{customdata:.3f}<br>x = %{x:.3f}<br>y = %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>"
      })
    }
    const layout = {
      xaxis: {title: "x", zeroline: true, range: [xRange.lo, xRange.hi], constrain: "domain"},
      // scaleanchor keeps one unit of y the same length on screen as one
      // unit of x -- without it a circle plots as an ellipse, which ruins
      // every curve below.
      //
      // constrain: "domain" -- on both axes, or the unconstrained one still
      // gets widened -- makes Plotly satisfy that by shrinking the drawn
      // plot area to the curve's own aspect ratio, leaving the ranges above
      // exactly as asked for. The default ("range") instead widens
      // whichever range is too tight for the box -- and since newPlot runs
      // on a still-detached div (Plotly measures its 700x450 default) while
      // every later react runs at the real size, the two widened by
      // different amounts and the first slider nudge visibly jumped the
      // zoom. Pinning the ranges removes the discrepancy at the source.
      yaxis: {title: "y", zeroline: true, range: [yRange.lo, yRange.hi], scaleanchor: "x", scaleratio: 1, constrain: "domain"},
      hovermode: "closest",
      uirevision: key,
      autosize: true
    }
    const config = VM.plotting.config()

    if (!_plotDiv) {
      _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
      _plotDiv.className = "plotly-box-large"
      Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
      VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)
    } else {
      Plotly.react(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
    }
    return _plotDiv
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// The slider steps by one sample of plotterSetup, so its value doubles as
// an index into the sampled arrays -- see plotterMainPlot's cursor trace.
plotterCursorIndex = {
  if (plotterSetup.ts.length === 0) return null
  const span = plotterSetup.tMax - plotterSetup.tMin
  const index = Math.round((plotterT - plotterSetup.tMin) / span * (plotterSetup.ts.length - 1))
  return index
}
```

```{ojs}
// Always-live: the cursor moves as the slider is dragged, no Plot click
// needed. Recreated whenever a new curve is committed, so its range always
// spans that curve's own t interval.
viewof plotterT = {
  const {tMin, tMax} = plotterSetup

  // Round the step to the nearest 1/2/5 x 10^k below span/500, so the
  // slider's own number readout stays short (0.05, not 0.0157145109...)
  // whatever t-range the current curve happens to span.
  const raw = (tMax - tMin) / 500
  const magnitude = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(raw)))
  const normalized = raw / magnitude
  let nice
  if (normalized <= 1) nice = 1
  else if (normalized <= 2) nice = 2
  else if (normalized <= 5) nice = 5
  else nice = 10
  const step = nice * magnitude

  const slider = Inputs.range([tMin, tMax], {label: "t", step, value: tMin})
  slider.classList.add("ojs-fill")
  // Opts this slider into the play/pause button (js/ui/slider-play.js), so
  // the point can be watched tracing the curve rather than dragged along it.
  slider.dataset.vmPlay = ""
  return slider
}
```
